verdict.rationale: CoreWeave documents provisioning GPU compute through CKS: clusters can be created via the Cloud Console, Terraform, or the CKS API, and GPU Node Pools (including pay-as-you-go Spot) run inside them. Code then runs through a generated kubeconfig and kubectl, and the pricing page claims you can quickly spin up on-demand capacity. However, the unit is a managed Kubernetes cluster and Node Pool on bare metal rather than a standalone instance, and nothing evidences how long it takes to go from request to running code. Missing for 10: documented time-to-first-workload (minutes), standalone on-demand instance provisioning outside the Kubernetes cluster model, an API-driven Node Pool creation walkthrough, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can provision an on-demand GPU instance from the console or API and be running code on it within minutes

citations.quote: You can create a cluster with the Cloud Console or with Terraform.
The API lets you create, list, update, and delete managed Kubernetes clusters on CoreWeave infrastructure.
Quickly spin-up burst On-Demand or Spot capacity—with the flexibility of great pricing.
Spot Node Pools provide pay-as-you-go access to high-performance bare-metal compute resources without long-term commitments or reservations.
Create and download a kubeconfig for a specific cluster, so you can interact with the cluster using commands like kubectl.
